summary_paragraph: A 65-year-old man with primary central nervous system B-cell lymphoma was admitted electively for his 27th cycle of high-dose methotrexate chemotherapy. His white blood cell count had previously been low due to increased alcohol use, but it had recovered to a safe level for treatment. The chemotherapy infusion was completed without complications. An EEG was performed during admission, showing mild focal slowing in the left temporal region consistent with prior brain surgery and tumor site, but no epileptiform discharges. Methotrexate levels were monitored and decreased appropriately, allowing for safe discharge. The patient was instructed to continue leucovorin and sodium bicarbonate for three days post-discharge, increase lamotrigine to 50 mg twice daily for seizure prophylaxis, and follow up with his oncologist to review EEG results and plan future therapy. He was discharged home in stable condition.
